text:
[LSER.17.2] The applicability matrix:

| Aggregation | Slot value types | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `min`, `max` | `Float`, `Int`, `Duration` | the slot's type, nullable |
| `sum` | `Float`, `Int`, `Duration` | the slot's type |
| `mean`, `median`, `variance`, `stdev`, `pvariance`, `pstdev`, `pXX` | `Float`, `Int`, `Duration` | `Float?` |
| `count` | any sampled type | `Int` |
| `count_distinct` | any sampled type | `Int` |
| `count_of` | any sampled type | `Int` |
| `contains` | any sampled type | `Bool` |
| `bool_and`, `bool_or` | `Bool` only | `Bool?` |
| `first`, `last` | any sampled type | the slot's type, nullable |
| `rate` | `Float`, `Int`, `Duration` | `Float?` |
| `direction` | `Float`, `Int`, `Duration` | `Int?` — `-1`, `0` or `+1` |

The sampled types are `Float`, `Int`, `Bool`, `String`, `Time`, `Date` and
`Duration`, a unit-typed slot, and an opaque type over any of them. No row admits
any other slot ([LSER.17.4], [LSER.17.5]).

**`Returns` is the static type of both call forms** — `<agg>(cursor)`
([LSER.16.1]) and the companion slot ([LSER.6]) — so every downstream check
over the value has a type to work with. A nullable return is `null` exactly when
the read is cold ([LSER.19.8]), for `direction`, `variance` and `stdev` also when
the window holds one sample ([LSER.10.9], [LSER.16.3.3]), and for `rate` also when no time elapses between the
window's first and last samples ([LSER.16.9]); the others answer their concrete
cold value.

**The statistical family returns `Float` whatever the slot holds**, `median`
and `pXX` included: `p50` of an `Int` slot's `[1, 2]` is `1.5`. They
interpolate rather than select an observed value, which is what makes the
column a function of the aggregation alone and needs no tie-break rule.
`min`, `max`, `first` and `last` preserve the slot's type because they *do*
select an observed value.

**Over a slot of the `time` dimension ([LTIM.1.3.5]) `mean`, `median`, `stdev`,
`pstdev` and `pXX` return `Duration?`.** The engine computes the `Float` this
clause states, and the result rounds as a `Duration` scaled by a `Float` does
([LTIM.4.1.1]). `variance` and `pvariance` stay `Float?`.

**`pXX` interpolates linearly between the two order statistics that bracket
it, and `median` is `p50`.** $p$ is the integer `XX`. The engine sorts the
window's $n$ samples ascending as `Float`, an `Int` sample converting
round-to-nearest-even and $-0$ ordering before $+0$, giving
$x_0 \le \dots \le x_{n-1}$. In exact integers:

$\mathit{num} = (n-1)\,p, \quad \mathit{lo} = \lfloor \mathit{num}/100 \rfloor, \quad \mathit{frac} = \mathit{num} \bmod 100$

The result is $x_{\mathit{lo}}$ when $\mathit{frac} = 0$, when
$x_{\mathit{lo}} = x_{\mathit{lo}+1}$, or when $x_{\mathit{lo}} = -\infty$ and
$x_{\mathit{lo}+1} \ne +\infty$. Otherwise it is

$x_{\mathit{lo}} + \frac{\mathit{frac}}{100}\,(x_{\mathit{lo}+1} - x_{\mathit{lo}})$

and the engine **must** evaluate it as correctly rounded IEEE-754 operations in
exactly this order: the subtraction, the division $\mathit{frac}/100$, the
multiplication, the addition. A cold window ($n = 0$) reads `null`
([LSER.19.8]); $n = 1$ reads $x_0$. A window holding both $-\infty$ and
$+\infty$ as the bracketing pair reads NaN, which no slot admits ([LEXP.4.2]).

`sum` preserves the slot's type, so an `Int` slot accumulates in a 64-bit
signed integer and wraps per [LSER.16.2.2]; summing a `Float` slot is the
stated way to trade exactness for magnitude range.

The three signal aggregations are not in this matrix; [LSIG.1.1] carries
their element types, time models and returns together.
